messages:
rachael: quick check — I hit an odd shape from /v1/chat/completions when streaming + tool calling. small repro below, can someone confirm intended contract?

ben: can you paste the minimal streaming fragments you saw?

rachael: sure — simplified stream chunks we get:
```json
{\"delta\": {\"role\": \"assistant\"}}
{\"delta\": {\"content\": \"Processing...\"}}
{\"delta\": {\"tool_call\": {\"name\": \"lookup\", \"arguments\": \"{\\\"q\\\":\\\"id:123\\\"}\"}}}
{\"delta\": {\"content\": \"Result:\"}}
{\"finish_reason\": null}
```

rachael: then the non-streaming (final) response body we see in the same client is missing `role` inside `choices[0].message` (only content + tool_call info). so two questions: 1) should final non-streaming response always have `message.role` set if any streamed chunk had role? 2) is it OK for `tool_call` to appear both in streaming `delta` and as `message.tool_call` in final payload (duplication)?

ben: my take — final response should be canonical and self-contained, so yes, role should be present. streaming deltas can be partial. duplication of tool_call is okay but we should document that fields in final message are authoritative.

tim: +1 to ben. also note SDK layer should probably normalize/merge deltas into a single message object before handing to app code. we used to have a bug where role came as a separate event and some clients set role=null.

rachael: that makes sense. do we have an open spec line for this? seems like a small contract clarification (role nullability + duplication semantics).

ben: not sure. I can open a tiny PR to the convo contract doc to state: 
- streaming deltas are incremental and may include `role` once
- final non-streaming `choices[0].message.role` MUST be present when role was sent in stream
- `tool_call` may be repeated in stream; final message is authoritative

dev-bot: Created issue #1234: "convo: clarify streaming delta -> final message normalization (role/tool_call)" and linked to convo-contract board.

rachael: awesome, thanks. I'll add a short repro and request review from @tim and @ben. :thumbsup:
